messages:
alex: heads-up — automated canary traffic shift just failed during the subnet rebalance in eu-west-2. Seeing 502s and connection resets from the canary pods after splitter flip.
sam: saw alerts. Istio logs show a bunch of connection refused between sidecars and redis-backed cache. Could be new pods landing on a different subnet with stricter sg rules.
priya: gitops-bot shows no reconciles failed but terraform drift alert popped: terraform workspace 'prod' wanted to move 2/6 worker subnets to new id. Looks like cloud autoscaler triggered rebalance mid-rollout.
gitops-bot: Reconcile summary: apps/canary-service (helmRelease) succeeded at 1965432085. No pending changes in kustomize overlay. Terraform drift detected: aws_subnet.* planned_replace true.
jonathan: the rollout automation (traffic-splitter v1.3) tried to ramp to 20% but health probes started failing at ~5% because those canary pods had new ENIs in subnet-b that had stricter egress NAT rules.
maya_ops: confirmed: NAT gateway routing table for subnet-b missing the 0.0.0.0/0 route after the IPAM shrink. That explains egress failures to the feature toggle service.
alex: oof. So sequence: subnet rebalance (cloud autoscaler/terraform) -> new pods scheduled -> network path broken -> canary traffic ramp -> failures -> canary automation marks unhealthy and triggers rollback, but our rollback helm hook failed due to preStop race.
sam: logs from deploy-bot: "rollback triggered for canary-service v2026.03.18-7 but helm rollback hook timed out: preStop waiting for graceful shutdown timed out, pod stuck Terminating and not evicted."
priya: can anyone run this to manually restore traffic split? I think we should immediately cut traffic back to stable to avoid user impact and then pin the nodepool so IPAM stops rebalancing during rollouts.
jonathan: commands to run:

kubectl -n platform get trafficsplit canary-splitter -o yaml
# then patch
kubectl -n platform patch trafficsplit canary-splitter --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/backends/0/weight","value":"100"},{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/backends/1/weight","value":"0"}]'

deploy-bot: traffic-split patch applied at 1965432250. Observability: 5xxs dropping, stable latency back to normal.
maya_ops: rolling update for affected nodegroup to reattach correct route table. Terraform plan shows subnet replacement in progress; I'll pause the gitops terraform apply for that workspace to avoid finishing the replacement mid-cutover.
alex: quick risk/cost note — autoscaler moved a bunch of spot instances out; we had to spin up ondemand which bumped cost ~+18% for the hour. Flagging for finance follow-up.
sam: follow-ups: 1) Add a pre-deploy guard in the canary pipeline to fail if any terraform plans include subnet replacement 2) Update rollback hook timeout to avoid stuck Terminating pods 3) Add a temporary hold on autoscaler during staged traffic shifts 4) Add network e2e in canary smoke to validate NAT/egress (call to feature-toggle + redis) before shifting traffic.
priya: I'll open the GH issue and a runbook note. Putting myself on the action to add the pre-deploy guard.
jonathan: FYI I'll create a quick ops playbook snippet to recover earlier: include kubectl patch, how to detect stalled preStop, and how to force delete pods if needed (kubectl delete pod --grace-period=0 --force).
alex: thanks team. We'll do a retro tomorrow. For now the canary remains stopped and traffic at 100% stable. :thumbsup:
